sections.title: Sec 1: Understanding Refraction
lecture_lines: Light travels straight until it hits water.
It slows down and bends at the boundary.
This bending is called refraction.
The angle determines how much it bends.
Understanding this is key to lenses.
animations: Animation step 1: Draw a straight white line (#FFFFFF) representing light traveling from left to right on a black background (#000000).
Animation step 2: Fade in a blue rectangle (#4488CC) on the right side to represent water. The light line stops at the boundary.
Animation step 3: Animate the light line bending downwards as it enters the blue rectangle. Change the line color to light yellow (#FFFF99) to indicate speed change.
Animation step 4: Draw a dashed vertical line (#888888) at the boundary labeled 'Normal'. Show the angle between the incoming ray and normal, then the angle between the refracted ray and normal.
Animation step 5: Flash the word 'Refraction' in bright cyan (#00FFFF) at the center of the screen.

sections.title: Sec 2: The Shape of the Convex Lens
lecture_lines: A convex lens is thick in the middle.
It is thin at the edges.
Light travels slower in glass.
Center light takes a longer path.
This path difference causes bending.
animations: Animation step 1: Draw a biconvex lens shape using two curved lines meeting at points, filled with semi-transparent light blue (#ADD8E6).
Animation step 2: Draw a horizontal red line (#FF4444) through the center (optical axis) and a vertical green line (#44FF44) through the middle (center of lens).
Animation step 3: Highlight the central vertical section of the lens in bright orange (#FFA500) to show thickness. Label it 'Thick Center'.
Animation step 4: Highlight the top and bottom edges of the lens in bright purple (#9400D3). Label them 'Thin Edges'.
Animation step 5: Animate a white dot moving from the center of the lens to the edge, with a trail that gets shorter, illustrating the path length difference.

sections.title: Sec 3: Bending the Rays: The Mechanism
lecture_lines: Parallel rays enter the lens from the left.
Top rays bend downward toward the axis.
Bottom rays bend upward toward the axis.
The central ray goes straight through.
Curvature acts like angled mirrors.
animations: Animation step 1: Draw three parallel horizontal white lines (#FFFFFF) entering the lens from the left: one top, one middle, one bottom.
Animation step 2: Animate the top ray hitting the left surface of the lens. It bends sharply downward as it crosses into the glass.
Animation step 3: Animate the bottom ray hitting the left surface of the lens. It bends sharply upward as it crosses into the glass.
Animation step 4: Animate the middle ray passing straight through the center without bending. Keep the middle ray white.
Animation step 5: As the rays exit the right side of the lens, they bend again (inward) to converge. Flash the lens outline in bright yellow (#FFFF00) to emphasize the curvature's role.

sections.title: Sec 4: Convergence at the Focal Point
lecture_lines: All refracted rays meet at one point.
This point is called the Focal Point.
It lies on the principal axis.
Distance from lens is the Focal Length.
We label this distance as f.
animations: Animation step 1: Continue the ray paths from Section 3. Show the top, middle, and bottom rays intersecting at a single point on the right side of the lens.
Animation step 2: Place a bright red dot (#FF0000) at the intersection point. Label it 'F' in white text.
Animation step 3: Draw a double-headed arrow from the center of the lens to point F. Color the arrow cyan (#00FFFF).
Animation step 4: Label the arrow with the letter 'f' in large, bold white font.
Animation step 5: Flash the entire path of the rays in green (#00FF00) briefly to show the complete convergence process.

sections.title: Sec 5: Real-World Application: The Magnifying Glass
lecture_lines: Magnifying glasses focus sunlight to a point.
Energy concentrates at the focal point.
This high intensity can burn paper.
This is how real images form.
Understanding focus explains many optical tools.
animations: Animation step 1: Draw a simple magnifying glass icon (circle with handle) in light gray (#D3D3D3) on the left.
Animation step 2: Animate parallel yellow rays (#FFFF00) entering the magnifying glass from the left, converging to a point on the right.
Animation step 3: Place a small brown square (#8B4513) at the focal point to represent paper. The rays converge exactly on this square.
Animation step 4: Animate a small puff of gray smoke (#A9A9A9) rising from the paper square, indicating burning.
Animation step 5: Fade out the rays and smoke, leaving the magnifying glass and the label 'Focus = Energy' in white text.
